title: The Island Queen excursion steamer
summary: The sidewheeler Island Queen made daily Cincinnati excursions to Coney Island and an autumn trip to New Orleans, with a Paducah band living aboard for $40 a week room and board.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: And so while I was doing this a guy come through there, the boat come through, the Island Queen, and it stayed in Cincinnati. A beautiful boat, a big sidewheeler, you know.

And what it did, every -- around the summer, it would take excursions from Cincinnati to a park about 12 miles out of Cincinnati called Coney Island. And this boat would take excursions every day out there, and then around the middle of September, it would take a trip from Cincinnati all the way down the Ohio River into the Mississippi River and then to New Orleans.

Yeah, paddlewheel. Playing excursions on each side. See, like Cincinnati, and then it would come down to New Albany, which is across the river, and then it would play on the other side, Louisville, Kentucky, then it would go all the way down and play the -- it would go all the way down and

stop at Paducah. Now, this band that I'm telling you about, that was playing the boat, they were from Paducah, Kentucky, and what happened, you'd get down to Memphis, and at Memphis the Ohio River pours right into the Mississippi.
Then you've got Memphis, play there, like a moonlight excursion. You'd go out at night about 8:00 o'clock and they'd get back at 12:00, the dance.
Well, all those excursions you talked about, they'd go out and come back, bring the people back to where they took them from.
Yeah, go out and bring them back.
And then start off for the next town. And you know --
What did the band do? Where did they sleep?
Sleep right on the boat and eat right on the boat. $40.00 a week, room and board. So the guys would come through there, and that was a lot of money at that time, you know.
